source_caption:
During the massive anti-war rally sequence at the Lincoln Memorial in Forrest Gump, a military official sabotages the sound system, unplugging the audio cables right as Forrest is asked to speak about his combat experience in Vietnam. Although the film’s audience cannot hear his speech over the muted PA system, Tom Hanks actually recited a fully scripted line into the dead microphone: “Sometimes when people go to Vietnam, they go home to their mommas without any legs. Sometimes they don’t go home at all. That’s a bad thing. That’s all I have to say about that.” Director Robert Zemeckis chose to silence the audio in the final edit to emphasize how Forrest’s simple, unvarnished truth was muted by political noise, making Jenny’s immediate recognition of his voice from across the Reflecting Pool all the more emotionally powerful.

Forrest Gump (1994), directed by Robert Zemeckis, starring Tom Hanks, Robin Wright, Gary Sinise, Sally Field. A kind-hearted, slow-witted Alabama man unwittingly witnesses and influences pivotal historical events of the 20th century, all while maintaining a lifelong, unwavering love for his troubled childhood sweetheart.

source_details.synopsis: Forrest Gump is a 1994 American comedy-drama film directed by Robert Zemeckis. An adaptation of the 1986 novel of the same name by Winston Groom, the film's screenplay was written by Eric Roth. It stars Tom Hanks in the title role, alongside Robin Wright, Gary Sinise, Mykelti Williamson, and Sally Field in lead roles. The film follows the life of an Alabama man named Forrest Gump (Hanks) and his experiences in the 20th-century United States. Principal photography took place between August and December 1993, mainly in the tri-states Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina.
